sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining in Xenopus oocytes: WT HA-tagged KCNQ5 shows normal plasma membrane localization; G278S mutant shows reduced surface signal. Electrophysiological function of the HA-tagged WT construct is not explicitly reported in the ledger clip.
sites.rationale: L1 is the sole ledger entry and confirms that an extracellular HA tag on full-length, membrane-anchored KCNQ5 is tolerated and surface-detectable. KCNQ5 has no extracellular terminus (N-term residues 1-126 are intracellular; C-term residues 346-932 are intracellular), so the tag must reside in one of the three extracellular loops (ECL1 148-158, ECL2 220-224, ECL3 287-326). Because the paper names neither a loop nor a residue, no junction can be derived without structural inference, which is prohibited; insert_after_residue is therefore null. Python verification confirms that canonical position 278 is Ile, not Gly, indicating the paper's G278S numbering reflects a shorter isoform, but this does not affect the tag-site evidence. Full-length KCNQ5 carrying an extracellular HA-tag was expressed in Xenopus oocytes (PMID 25649132). Both wild-type and G278S-mutant constructs were assessed for plasma membrane localization by surface immunostaining of the HA epitope, confirming the tag is extracellular and the WT construct is surface-displayed. The paper names no specific loop or residue for the HA insertion.

sources.claim: Indeed, when expressed in Xenopus oocytes, KCNQ5 G278S subunitscarryinganextracellularHA-tagdisplayed reduced plasma membrane localization compared with similarly tagged wild-type (WT) KCNQ5 (Supplementary Fig. 1c,d).

literature_notes: Only one ledger entry exists for KCNQ5 (L1, PMID 25649132). It confirms extracellular HA tagging of full-length KCNQ5 in Xenopus oocytes but names no specific loop or residue. KCNQ5 has three extracellular loops (ECL1 S1-S2: 148-158, 11 aa; ECL2 S3-S4: 220-224, 5 aa; ECL3 pore: 287-326, 40 aa) and no extracellular terminus, so topology_derived does not apply. The site is reported at region level with null insert_after_residue. The paper's G278S mutation maps to Ile-278 in the canonical 932-aa sequence (TM5), indicating the paper uses a shorter isoform; this discrepancy does not affect the HA-tag evidence. No intracellular or function-abrogating positions are named in the ledger.
